$comment: THE LICENCE REGISTER — a RECORD, not a gate.
D12b: this project imports everything each atlas offers, stays open source and
non-commercial, and renders every attribution its sources require. Nothing is
excluded on licence grounds. What this file does is keep the licence position
knowable, so it can be reviewed properly before publication instead of guessed.
`npm run check:licences` reads the SHIPPED GLBs — including the per-structure
component tags build-z-anatomy.mjs writes into them — and regenerates
docs/LICENCE_LOG.md. Read the log, not this file, for the current state; this
file holds the things a machine cannot derive from an asset: why a source was
chosen, what is unverified, and what is closed by contract.
`verify` fields become checkboxes on the log's pre-publication action list.

tiers.note: Retained as vocabulary for the log, NOT as an exclusion mechanism. D12 briefly used these to gate a publish step and D12b replaced that with the record-keeping approach. They remain useful for saying what an obligation IS.

open.obligation: Attribution, and share-alike where the licence says so. No barrier to publishing.

non-commercial.obligation: Attribution, plus the project must not be sold. Compatible with this project's stated stance. ⚠️ It does mean the bundled result cannot be offered under a licence that permits commercial reuse — the NC parts stay NC, so the whole is 'open source, non-commercial' rather than Open Definition conformant. Say so plainly when publishing.

no-licence.obligation: NO GRANT EXISTS. Attribution satisfies a licence's conditions; it cannot manufacture permission that was never given. Needs written permission from the rights holder, or replacement geometry, before publication.

closed.obligation: Not reachable by any decision of ours — a contract with someone else.

assets.attribution: Z-Anatomy - The open source atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0; incl. Anatomy of the Inner Ear by University of Dundee School of Medicine (CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0), itself a derivative of '3D Ear' by W. Robert J. Funnell, Sam Daniel and Daren Nicholson at McGill University used under CC-BY-NC-SA 1.0; Cranial Nerves and Foramina by University of Dundee, CAHID, produced by Sophia Lappe, used with permission, based on the BodyParts3D data set, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution 4.0 International; Kidney by lissiecowley (CC-BY-NC 4.0); and white matter boundary surfaces from Brain for Blender by Anderson M. Winkler, brainder.org (CC-BY-SA 3.0); derived from BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan.
assets.why:
All seven system files imported (D12b). Per-structure component tags live in the asset's own structure table, so docs/LICENCE_LOG.md counts what actually ships. AS OF 17 AUGUST 2026 (D20) THE PUBLISHABLE AND RESEARCH BUILDS ARE THE SAME BUILD: 3,617 structures, nothing excluded. 3,607 are Z-Anatomy's own CC BY-SA 4.0 work, 8 come from two non-commercial components (4 Dundee inner ear, 4 lissiecowley kidney), and 2 — the white matter boundary surfaces of the cerebral hemispheres — are Brain for Blender (Anderson M. Winkler, CC BY-SA 3.0), restored after three weeks excluded under upstream's wrong 'University of Washington, no licence' credit. Earlier counts for the record: 3,614 while the white matter was excluded; 3,626 before a zero-vertex-part guard stopped emitting nine empty structures; 8 tagged Dundee structures before the inner-ear pattern was narrowed to exclude the middle ear.

⚠️ THERE IS A FOURTH THIRD-PARTY COMPONENT AND IT WILL NOT APPEAR IN THE COMPONENTS TABLE: 'Cranial Nerves and Foramina' (University of Dundee, CAHID, CC BY 4.0), listed in Z-Anatomy's own Resources/Models/License.txt alongside the other three. It is credited — in the attribution above, in the asset's embedded copyright, and in-app by AtlasAttribution — but it is deliberately NOT tagged per structure, because Dundee's nerve geometry and Z-Anatomy's own are not separable by name and a guessed pattern once caught the cochlear NERVE along with the cochlea (docs/PLAN_NEXT.md item 3). The table is built from tags, so a missing row there means 'not tagged', never 'not in this asset'. ⚠️ It was absent from this attribution and from build-z-anatomy.mjs's COPYRIGHT until 17 August 2026 while the interface rendered it — so the two credits that travel WITH the file were the two that omitted it, and attribution is a CONDITION of CC BY 4.0. Fixed in both, and written into the built GLBs with scripts/set-copyright.mjs rather than waiting for an FBX rebuild.

⚠️ BOTH DUNDEE COMPONENTS ARE THEMSELVES DERIVATIVES, AND WE CREDITED ONLY THE NEAREST LINK UNTIL 18 AUGUST 2026 (D23). Caroline Erolin (Reader in Medical Art, Dundee) answered our credit-wording query with the chains: the inner ear derives from '3D Ear' by W. Robert J. Funnell, Sam Daniel and Daren Nicholson at McGill University under CC BY-NC-SA 1.0; the cranial nerves were produced by Sophia Lappe and derive from BodyParts3D itself. Both now appear in the attribution above, in the embedded copyright and in the interface via RightsComponent.derivedFrom. Three things verification added that her mail did not say: McGill's host is DEAD, so the CC BY-NC-SA 1.0 statement is confirmed only from the Internet Archive; behind McGill is a further UNCREDITED layer — cadaver MRI from Drs O. W. Henson Jr and Miriam Henson (UNC Chapel Hill), scanned at Duke's Center for In Vivo Microscopy — which nobody in the chain credits and we cannot fix upstream; and CC ShareAlike 1.0 requires adaptations under EXACTLY 1.0 (the 'or later' clause arrives with 2.0), so Dundee's 1.0 -> 4.0 step is not a move that licence offers. None of that changes what governs OUR use: the NC term flows down under every reading and this project is non-commercial. ⚠️ ONE OPEN QUESTION, worth asking her rather than assuming: the Cranial Nerves and Foramina Sketchfab page states NO LICENCE AT ALL (the API returns an empty licence object, as it does for every model on that account) — the CC BY 4.0 we print comes from Z-Anatomy's file, not from Dundee's page, and a sibling Dundee cranial-nerves model by Claire Cooper is listed CC BY-SA 4.0 elsewhere. Her reply neither confirmed nor disputed the licence; she was asked about wording.

⚠️ NoAI — MARKED ON THE CRANIAL NERVES, NOT ON THE INNER EAR (both pages checked 18 August 2026, and the asymmetry is real: only the CAHID model carries the badge). Sketchfab's marking forbids use 'in datasets for, in the development of, or as inputs to generative AI programs' (their terms, 23 March 2023). It does NOT restrict viewing, rendering or redistribution, which is the whole of what this viewer does with the geometry — it is converted by deterministic tooling (FBX to glTF, weld, decimate, meshopt, AO bake) and drawn. NOTHING HERE IS TRAINING DATA. That distinction deserves stating plainly rather than by implication, because this repository IS written by an AI agent: the agent writes the code and reads the licence files; the anatomy is data that code renders, never data a model consumes. Recorded as noAI on the component and rendered in-app so the creator's request travels with their work instead of stopping at the platform they posted it on.

components.verify: ⚠️ NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT, 18 August 2026 — one branch eliminated, one remains. Contains Incus, Stapes and Malleus, untagged, i.e. credited as Z-Anatomy's own. The comparison run for docs/OUTREACH.md item 2 established they CANNOT be BodyParts3D retopologies: the imported BodyParts3D set has no ossicles at all, and TARO is a 2 mm MRI phantom that physically cannot resolve millimetre-scale bones. So they are either Z-Anatomy's own modelling or part of Dundee's ear component. We credit them as Z-Anatomy's on the middle-ear/inner-ear distinction (Dundee's component is 'Anatomy of the INNER Ear'; ossicles are middle ear, and they sit in the SKELETON file); upstream is asked to correct us if that is wrong.

components.note: Never licence-blocked — plain CC BY-SA, simply unbuilt until 28 July. ⚠️ Note the version suffix is 41, not 100 like every other file. Z-Anatomy's convention appears to encode completeness, so this may be a partial model. Check coverage before trusting it.

components.licence: MIXED — mostly CC BY-SA 4.0, plus the CC BY-NC-SA inner ear and the CC BY-SA 3.0 Brainder boundary surfaces
components.note: ⚠️ docs/ROADMAP.md Phase 3 warned this file was not uniformly CC BY-SA and was RIGHT. It carries the CC BY-NC-SA Dundee inner ear (Cochlea and Vestibule per side; the middle-ear structures first swept in were removed from the tag) and the white-matter meshes upstream credited to 'the University of Washington' with no licence. D20 resolved that credit: the telencephalon pair is the Brain for Blender grey/white boundary surface (Anderson M. Winkler, CC BY-SA 3.0, tagged white-matter-brainder), the spinal-cord tube is Z-Anatomy's own and is untagged, and UW — which the named source denies any affiliation with — appears nowhere. ⚠️ The cochlear and vestibular NERVES and NUCLEI are Z-Anatomy's own and are deliberately NOT tagged — only the sense organ is Dundee's. Tagging the nerves would over-attribute.

Never licence-blocked — plain CC BY-SA, simply unbuilt. Spleen, thymus, palatine tonsil and ~106 lymph node groups. SystemId has no 'lymphoid' and deliberately still does not: the meshes carry system 'lymphoid' in extras, systemForGroup returns null, and AtlasBody renders them unresolved — visible and named but not score-coloured. Adding a SystemId would have drifted the health-data contract (D8 owns it upstream) for a geometry reason.

Contains the CC BY-NC 4.0 kidney (lissiecowley), imported and tagged per structure. Also the one file where 'one FBX per system' breaks down: viscera span digestive, respiratory, endocrine, reproductive and urinary, so the system comes from the mesh name via visceralSystem() rather than the filename. urinary maps to 'metabolic', matching the FMA walk already recorded in docs/bodyparts3d-system-map.tsv.

Imported 28 July as its own asset (z-anatomy-regions), not merged into the body. Surface regions lie on the skin and would hide every organ behind them; as a separate atlas source it is one click in the switcher. Never a licence question — plain CC BY-SA.

assets.verify: ✅ THE DISTRIBUTION GATE IS CLEAR (D20, 17 August 2026) — for three weeks this field said the University of Washington white matter had no licence and blocked it from every served build. Resolved by asking the named source and measuring the geometry: Anderson M. Winkler (Brainder, brainder.org) denies any UW affiliation, ever; the telencephalon pair measures as his project's grey/white BOUNDARY surface (closed folded hemispheres, sphericity 0.219, exact mirrors of one source hemisphere) and is tagged white-matter-brainder at CC BY-SA 3.0, distributable inside this CC BY-SA 4.0 asset per BY-SA 3.0 §4(b); the spinal-cord tube (open, smooth, cortex-only Brainder cannot be its source) is Z-Anatomy's own and untagged. Nothing in this asset is excluded by --publishable any more. TWO THINGS REMAIN OPEN, NEITHER GATING: Winkler's confirmation from the renders sent 17 August decides the credit WORDING (docs/OUTREACH.md item 3 — if he unexpectedly disowns the pair, it reverts to Z-Anatomy's own CC BY-SA 4.0, still licensed); and upstream's licence file still carries the wrong UW credit, raised with Z-Anatomy in OUTREACH item 2 so the error stops propagating. ⚠️ UPDATE 18 August 2026 (D23b) — THE CAHID CRANIAL NERVES CARRY NO CC LICENCE, and we printed CC BY 4.0 for weeks on Z-Anatomy's say-so. Caroline Erolin confirmed in writing: the model is not downloadable from their Sketchfab page so no licence was ever attached, and the licence its description states is the licence of the DATA IT IS BASED ON. She gave express permission for this project — 'As this is based on the open-source Body Parts 3D data I don't have a problem with it being re-purposed for this project' — and supplied the attribution she wants, which names the BodyParts3D chain. The in-app credit now reads 'used with permission' and names that chain rather than asserting a CC grant nobody made. ⚠️ SHE ALSO CORROBORATED THE DBCLS RELICENCE INDEPENDENTLY: checking the BodyParts3D page for this reply, she found it now states CC BY 4.0 where it said CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan when she published five years ago. That is a second party arriving at the same reading as docs/OUTREACH.md item 5, which is not written confirmation from DBCLS but is no longer only our own inference. ⚠️ The INNER EAR chain is not hers: Dundee's medical school holds that model, and she referred the McGill/UNC/Duke question to Eve Laws there.

assets.attribution: Z-Anatomy - The open source atlas of anatomy - CC-BY-SA 4.0; derived from BodyParts3D - The Database Center for Life Science - CC-BY-SA 2.1 Japan.
assets.why:
Surface topography from Regions of human body100.fbx — 256 named regions of the body surface. Plain CC BY-SA with none of the four third-party components, so it is the cleanest asset in the set. A SEPARATE GLB for a geometric reason, not a licence one: the patches lie on the skin and would occlude every organ if merged into z-anatomy.

⚠️ ITS EMBEDDED COPYRIGHT SAID OTHERWISE UNTIL 17 AUGUST 2026. build-z-anatomy.mjs wrote one aggregate string into both assets, so this file claimed a non-commercial inner ear, a non-commercial kidney and an unlicensed white matter that are not in it. That is over-attribution, which marks geometry as more restricted than it is — the same error the inner-ear tag made in the other direction. The script now writes a narrower COPYRIGHT_REGIONS matching this attribution, and the built files were corrected with scripts/set-copyright.mjs.

assets.attribution: CT from the ENHANCE.PET 1.6k dataset, subject 1032 (University Hospital Leipzig contribution, CC BY 4.0); segmented with MOOSE 3.2 (ENHANCE-PET), CC BY 4.0 weights; meshed for this project.
assets.citation: Ferrara, D., Pires, M., Gutschmayer, S., et al. Sharing a whole-/total-body [18F]FDG-PET/CT dataset with CT-derived segmentations: an ENHANCE.PET initiative. Scientific Data (2026). doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07218-y
assets.why:
Built by the MOOSE pipeline from ENHANCE.PET subject 1032. THE SOURCE SCAN WAS NEVER RECORDED AT BUILD TIME — for three weeks this was the register's one unresolved entry, 'a record we failed to keep, not a party we failed to ask' (report 05), and D21's withhold machinery kept it out of the public build. RE-IDENTIFIED 18 August 2026 (D22) from three independent fingerprints, none of them memory: (1) the scan geometry — subject 1032's NIfTI header reads 287 slices x 3.0 mm = 861.0 mm z-extent, and the shipped GLB's measured anatomy span is 0.861 m to the millimetre; (2) the class census — the pipeline doc's per-model found-class counts for subject 1032 sum to 110, the GLB's exact node count, including the same 15 absent peripheral-bone classes; (3) the documentary trail — docs/CT_ATLAS_PIPELINE.md developed on enhance_1032_F.nii.gz and measured its axis codes. The dataset's own PT-details.xlsx records subject 1032 as University Hospital Leipzig: F, 81.8 y, 59 kg, 1.56 m, lung cancer, FDG-PET/CT 2009 on a Siemens Sensation 16.

⚠️ PROPERTIES THAT TRAVEL WITH IT: one 81.8-year-old oncology patient's low-dose CT — not healthy reference anatomy and not a population; skull base to mid-thigh only (861 mm), arms raised, so no skull vault, forearms-in-part, and nothing below mid-femur; the brain mask is 1 mL. Say so wherever it is offered.

⚠️ `loaded` read FALSE until 8 August 2026 and was simply stale — kept as the record of why the log once understated exposure for exactly the wrong asset.
assets.verify: ✅ RESOLVED (D22). The licence chain is CC BY 4.0 end to end, each link verified at source on 18 August 2026: the Leipzig contribution to ENHANCE.PET 1.6k is CC BY 4.0 per the dataset paper (doi:10.1038/s41597-026-07218-y — only the AutoPET subset is CC BY-NC) and the AWS Open Data registry entry; subject 1032 is Leipzig per the dataset's own CT-details.xlsx and PT-details.xlsx; MOOSE 3.2 weights are CC BY 4.0. STILL TRUE: if the pipeline is ever re-run with TotalSegmentator's GATED subtasks (tissue_types, appendicular_bones, face), the output becomes non-commercial and needs its own id here. And record the subject id IN THE ASSET next time — this entry cost a forensic session because a filename was not written down.

assets.attribution: Segmentations from the TCIA Healthy-Total-Body-CTs collection (subject 003), CC BY 4.0; meshed for this project. doi:10.7937/NC7Z-4F76.
assets.why: The first complete FEMALE body in this repo, and the first atlas derived from a real person's CT rather than modelled. Verified at source rather than from a survey: the segmentations AND the clinical demographics are both CC BY 4.0, and only the CT images sit behind the NIH Controlled Data Access Policy -- which does not matter, because the images are not needed to build this. Subject 003 is F, 26, 1.7018 m, BMI 20.4, from the collection's own clinical spreadsheet. Closes ROADMAP Phase 6, which HRA could not: HRA's female donor has no skeleton above the pelvis.
assets.verify: Nothing outstanding on rights. Two properties must travel with any use of it, both recorded in docs/healthy-total-body-cts-crosswalk.tsv. Labels are GROUPED -- one Ribcage rather than 24 ribs, one Spine rather than 24 vertebrae, every long bone merging left and right -- and the images being restricted means it cannot be re-segmented finer. And it is low-dose non-contrast CT, so bone is trustworthy and soft tissue is not: D10's contrast objection applies to the organ masks. ⚠️ Do not re-run this with TotalSegmentator's gated subtasks; that would make the output non-commercial and it would need its own entry.

assets.why: First organ overlay rather than an atlas: one organ, its own donor, and a time dimension no atlas here has. Apache-2.0 verified from the repository's own LICENSE. Built by scripts/build-biv-heart.mjs from the committed demo output; see docs/PLAN_INTEGRATION.md (B6).
assets.verify: ✅ RESOLVED 18 August 2026 (D21) — this field said BLOCKS PUBLICATION for three weeks, on one precise question: which cohort is the bundled 'patient1' demo case, UK Biobank or CARDIOHANCE? Answered in writing by Joshua Dillon (corresponding author, Auckland Bioengineering Institute): it is a CARDIOHANCE participant, with LOCAL ETHICS APPROVAL TO SHARE ONLINE and NO RESTRICTIONS on further use. Requested credit: reference the GitHub repository and a biv-me paper — preferring the 2026 Medical Image Analysis paper (doi:10.1016/j.media.2026.104252) over the superseded FIMH 2025 one, which this register previously cited. The citation field above carries it verbatim; the attribution and the in-app credit name the cohort and the ethics basis. publishable flipped to true in src/scene/organOverlays.ts the same day. The Sunnybrook CC0 fallback (docs/INTEGRATION_CANDIDATES.md C3) is no longer needed and stays recorded only as history. What still travels with any use: ONE participant's heart, a different person from the body it sits inside, shown at their measured size — a property to state, not a rights question.

assets.licence: None required — generated by this project
assets.attribution: Schematic optical eye generated by open-twin-openXR from the published Arizona eye model (Schwiegerling). Geometry original to this project.
assets.why: THE ONLY ASSET HERE WITH NO UPSTREAM RIGHTS HOLDER. Generated from published radii, conic constants, thicknesses and refractive indices. Those are measurements, and measurements are not copyrightable expression, so the mesh is ours outright — no licence, no attribution chain, no provenance question. Crediting Schwiegerling for the parameters is courtesy and good scholarship, not a licence condition. This is the pattern to reach for whenever a structure is fully specified in the literature: generate it and own it.
assets.verify: Nothing to verify for rights. What DOES need saying every time it is shown: it is a SCHEMATIC OPTICAL model — cornea, lens and retina only, with no sclera, iris, ciliary body, extraocular muscles, optic nerve or vasculature. Correct as optics; not a substitute for an anatomical eye, and not a donor's.
assets.ownLicence: None required — generated by this project

assets.attribution: OpenEar library of 3D models of the human temporal bone (Sieber et al., MED-EL / University of Bern), CC BY 4.0. Surface colour baked from the same specimen's true-colour micro-slicing volume.
assets.why: The D4 texture pilot at 1/100th of Visible Human's cost (B3), and it ANSWERS D4: photographic tissue colour does survive this pipeline. The first asset here coloured by what the tissue looked like rather than by a palette we chose. Licence re-confirmed CC BY 4.0 from the Zenodo API. Specimen ZETA only, indexed and pulled member-by-member over HTTP range requests by scripts/remote-zip-index.mjs, which fetched 140 MB instead of 7.3 GB. Meshes are in RAS and the colour volume in LPS, so the shipped FlipXY.h5 — diag(-1,-1,1) — is the whole registration: 6,985 of 7,200 sampled vertices land inside the volume on non-black tissue. Placed by landmark fit rather than by eye — five structures common to it and Z-Anatomy, 1.27 mm RMS, and the same fit is what identified it as a RIGHT ear.
assets.verify: Nothing outstanding on rights, and the pipeline blocker is fixed: all 12 structures now carry baked photographic colour, and it renders as the `openear` organ overlay. Three properties travel with any use of it. It is ONE cadaveric RIGHT temporal bone, not a population. 71.5% of its surface has a colour source and the rest is neutral grey, because the micro-sliced block (~39.6 x 39.6 x 51.8 mm) is smaller than the scan -- grey means 'no source', never 'this colour', and the per-structure split is in the asset's own extras. And it is ~14% larger than Z-Anatomy's inner ear, left unscaled deliberately; see the note in src/scene/organOverlays.ts.
assets.holder: MED-EL / University of Bern (Sieber et al.)

assets.attribution: Inter typeface by Rasmus Andersson, SIL Open Font License 1.1.
assets.why: Self-hosted from the official Inter 4.1 release: web/InterVariable.woff2, the COMPLETE variable font, 344 KB. Not a Google subset — a subset carries a `unicode-range`, which does not merely describe the file but restricts which characters the face may render, so anything outside it falls back to system-ui silently. Audited 29 July 2026: `->` and `~=` appear in rendered strings and Inter has both, yet the latin subset was letting the system font draw them. public/fonts/OFL.txt is byte-identical to LICENSE.txt in that release.
assets.verify: RESOLVED — no external runtime fetch remains. Verified twice: no fonts.googleapis or fonts.gstatic reference in src/ or index.html, and a full network capture of the running app shows every request on localhost with /fonts/InterVariable.woff2 served 200. Kept as a record because re-adding a CDN font link would silently reopen a GDPR exposure — LG Muenchen I (3 O 17493/20) held the IP disclosure alone sufficient. The only characters that still fall back are the emoji and geometric icons Inter genuinely lacks, which is correct: self-hosting an emoji font is neither wanted nor generally licensed.

assets.why: three, r3f, drei, @react-three/xr, three-mesh-bvh, zustand, recharts and the whole build chain are permissive. Deliberately NOT enumerated here — a hand-written copy of the dependency tree is the thing that goes stale. Run `npx license-checker --summary` for the live answer.
assets.verify: Re-run the checker after any dependency bump. The one historical trap is @pmndrs/assets (CC0, fine) pulling a re-resolution of the whole pmndrs stack.

assets.attribution: ANNY, a free-to-use 3D human parametric model for all ages — NAVER LABS Europe / NAVER Corporation. Apache-2.0 code over CC0 shape assets derived from MakeHuman. Cite arXiv:2511.03589. Baked to static geometry by this repository; no scan of any person was used.
assets.why:
THE ONLY GEOMETRY HERE THAT IS NOT SOMEBODY'S BODY, and that is the point. Every atlas and every overlay in this register derives from a real donor — a cadaver, a scan, a segmented patient — and carries the provenance and consent questions that come with one. A parametric body is scan-free: it is generated from shape targets, so there is no donor, no consent chain and no re-identification surface. RESEARCH.md argues that is an ethical feature rather than a shortfall, and this register should say so rather than leave a blank where a donor line would be.

It exists to close D14: three of the seven atlases ship NO integumentary geometry, so the glass hull was unavailable on exactly the sources with the richest anatomy. An envelope is a skin, so the control works again. See D16.
assets.verify:
THREE LICENCE BUCKETS IN ONE PACKAGE, and recording only the headline Apache-2.0 would misstate what is on screen. The code is Apache-2.0 (NAVER Corporation); the MakeHuman-derived shape assets this geometry actually comes from are CC0-1.0; a SOMA topology ships alongside under Apache-2.0 and is NOT used by these bakes. All three are declared in src/scene/bodyEnvelopes.ts and rendered in-app.

⚠️ NEVER BAKE WITH topology="smpl" OR "smplx". Both trigger a RUNTIME download of a non-commercial archive from download.europe.naverlabs.com inside download_noncommercial_data() (anny/paths.py). Because it happens at runtime rather than at install time, A DEPENDENCY AUDIT DOES NOT CATCH IT. scripts/anny/bake.py hardcodes the safe topology and exposes no flag for it — keep it that way.

NOT A MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT. The shape space is artist priors from MakeHuman, not anthropometric ground truth, so no body-composition, ergonomic or health claim may be attached. And its rest pose is not any atlas's: measured on Z-Anatomy it spans 1.124 m across the arms against the atlas's 0.646 m, so it wraps the torso and not the limbs. The interface states that; keep it stated.
assets.holder: NAVER Corporation / NAVER LABS Europe (code); MakeHuman community (CC0 shape assets)

assets.why:
THE SAME MODEL AS THE FIVE ENVELOPES, SAMPLED RATHER THAN FIXED. The envelopes are five static bakes; this is ANNY's phenotype space itself, sampled at the model's own stops so the browser can interpolate between them and the six sliders are live. It backs the standalone `parametric` mode, which replaces the atlas rather than wrapping it — see D16a for why an adjustable outside over fixed organs was the wrong pairing to offer.

Registered separately from the envelopes because it is a different artefact with a different question attached: it is not a rendering of one body but the space all of them come from. The answer is the same — Apache-2.0 code over CC0 shape assets, no donor — but it is recorded rather than inferred.
assets.verify:
SAME THREE LICENCE BUCKETS AND THE SAME topology TRAP as the envelopes above; scripts/anny/bake_grid.py likewise hardcodes topology="anny" and exposes no flag for it.

⚠️ `race` IS DELIBERATELY NOT BAKED, though the model offers it. "african / asian / caucasian" as interpolable shape axes is a claim about human variation this project has no basis to make. `cupsize` and `firmness` are excluded separately, as body-shape controls on a rendered 3D body that is already a body-image surface. Six axes ship: gender, age, muscle, weight, height, proportions.

NOT A MEASUREMENT INSTRUMENT, and the sliders make that easier to forget than the fixed envelopes did. The interface shows height, volume, mass and BMI for the generated SURFACE; mass and BMI are derived from volume under one assumed uniform density and are properties of a shape, not of a person.

THE GRID CARRIES ITS OWN TOPOLOGY (.idx), and must keep doing so. It first borrowed the index buffer from anny-adult-f.glb, whose vertices meshopt reorders during compression — so the indices numbered a different vertex array and every triangle was scrambled. Invisible on screen: positions come from the grid, so height and every slider read exactly correct, and the vertex counts matched. Signed volume exposed it (0.56 L against 51.20 L). src/scene/annyGrid.test.ts pins it and bake_grid.py asserts on it.

assets.attribution: Anatomical definitions from the Foundational Model of Anatomy 5.1.0 (Structural Informatics Group, University of Washington, CC BY 4.0) and the Uberon multi-species anatomy ontology (CC BY 3.0). Each definition names its own source where it is shown.
assets.why: THE FIRST USER-VISIBLE PAYOFF OF THE ONTOLOGY WORK, and the only asset here that is text rather than geometry. Structures could be named and addressed (FMA:24477) but not explained; this file answers 'what is that?' for the terms whose ontology defines them. KEYED BY CURIE, NEVER BY NAME — a name-keyed file breaks on the next rebuild, while a term means the same thing across every atlas here, so one file serves all of them. Built offline into a static file because a runtime call to a third party would put a visitor's browser in touch with someone else's server, which is the exposure `inter-font` records being removed.
assets.verify: ⚠️ COVERAGE IS THE ONTOLOGIES' PROPERTY, NOT A BUG, and it is wildly uneven — measure with `node scripts/build-definitions.mjs --measure` rather than believing any number in prose. UBERON defines nearly everything it names, so the UBERON-keyed atlases come out near complete; FMA publishes definitions for only ~2,172 of its ~100,000 classes AND most of those sit on properties rather than anatomical classes, so the FMA-keyed atlases (Z-Anatomy, BodyParts3D) get their major organs and nothing finer. A structure without a definition shows none. ⚠️ Every definition is passed through scripts/claims/lexicon.mjs at BUILD time and dropped if it trips — ingesting outside prose would otherwise be a hole straight through the claim gate that D8/D15 exist to hold. ⚠️ FMA's licence was read from the LICENSE file shipped in the release itself (CC BY 4.0); secondary sources say CC BY 3.0 and are stale. ⚠️ UBERON is MULTI-SPECIES: its entries can carry cross-species taxon notes, and taking the first `description` put a note about ascidian hearts under the human heart. pickDefinition() drops notes; if a strange definition ever appears, that is the function to look at.
assets.holder: Structural Informatics Group, University of Washington (FMA); the Uberon consortium (UBERON)

closed.why: Terms forbid redistributing the content or 3D derivatives. Not reachable by D12 — this is a contract and a purchase, not a licence tier.
Signed MTA forbids sublicensing and redistribution, and derived results return to the holder. A decision of ours cannot relax an agreement with someone else.

stance: OPEN SOURCE, FULLY ATTRIBUTED, AND NOTHING IS EXCLUDED ON LICENCE GROUNDS. This project takes what each source offers, credits every one of them, and keeps an accurate account of what is inside. Commercial use is not a goal, so a non-commercial term (CC BY-NC, CC BY-NC-SA) costs this project nothing and is NOT a reason to drop a component — the obligation it carries is attribution, and attribution is rendered in-app and embedded in every asset. Copyleft is the same: share-alike and AGPL ask for source and onward terms, which an open-source project supplies anyway. ⚠️ THE ONE THING THIS STANCE CANNOT COVER, and it is not about commerce: geometry with NO LICENCE STATEMENT grants nothing at all. Silence is not permission, so it needs written permission rather than a credit line, and `--publishable` drops it. That is a question of whether a grant exists, not of what it permits. The point of this register is therefore DILIGENT DOCUMENTATION, not gatekeeping: say precisely which licence and which permissions apply to every asset, so anyone downstream can make their own call with the facts in front of them.
